For JDBC source module, use Spring JDBC template with configurable polling interval and SQL query
For Redis sink, use Jedis client library to interact with Redis server
For Kafka sink, use Kafka 0.8+ producer client to publish messages to Kafka brokers
For ZK security (U3), leverage Zookeeper's built-in SASL authentication and ACL features
For Trigger abstraction (U4), use interface-based extension points rather than abstract class to allow greater flexibility
For HTTPS support (U8), leverage Spring Boot 1.1.7's built-in SSL/TLS support instead of custom implementation
For e2e test fix (U7), investigate process management between grunt serve and protractor, likely related to process lifecycle or port conflicts
For custom module example (U5), create a simple but complete example module demonstrating all key extension points
Follow existing Spring XD module testing patterns (unit tests + integration tests with embedded servers)
assumptions: Spring XD build infrastructure, CI, and module test harness are already available and functional
External test dependencies (Redis server, Kafka broker, JDBC databases like H2/PostgreSQL, embedded Zookeeper) are available in the test environment
A single developer performs all work; no parallelization assumed
Spring Boot 1.1.7 SNAPSHOT is available and compatible with Spring XD for U8 implementation
Existing Module SPI is stable and does not require modifications for new modules
No major refactoring of existing Spring XD core is required to add the new modules
All user stories are independent and can be developed in isolation without significant cross-impact
Documentation refers to in-code Javadoc plus a wiki/reference page update
Effort estimates include coding, local testing, and self-review but exclude product management, deployment, and end-user support
JDBC source supports a single SQL query with basic polling; complex CDC-style features are out of scope
HTTPS implementation only covers Admin server endpoints; other transport-level security is out of scope
Trigger abstraction extension focuses on adding public interfaces; rewriting existing triggers is not required

activities.activity_description: Set up local development environment, clone Spring XD source, configure IDE, ensure required test dependencies (Redis, Kafka, JDBC, ZK) are accessible, and verify build runs end-to-end.
Design the JDBC source module: define module options (query, polling interval, datasource URL/credentials), decide on per-message vs. batch ingestion, and design the option metadata.
Implement the JDBC source module Java class, wire Spring JDBC template, implement polling loop, map result sets to Messages, and register the module metadata.
Write unit tests for row-to-message mapping and integration tests against H2/PostgreSQL covering happy path, empty result sets, and query errors.
Design the Redis sink module: choose Jedis vs. Lettuce, define options (host, port, key expression, value serialization), and decide supported data structures (key/value).
Implement the Redis sink module, including connection management, payload-to-bytes serialization, and writing to Redis with configured key.
Write unit tests with an embedded Redis (or mocked Jedis) and an integration test that writes messages and verifies they appear in Redis.
Design how ZK authentication and ACL will be integrated with Spring XD: SASL scheme, credential propagation, and how container/Admin server present credentials.

activities.activity_name: U3 - Implement ZK ACL and authentication
activities.activity_description: Implement ZK authentication in the Curator/ZK client wrapper used by Spring XD, create zNodes with appropriate ACLs, and provide hooks for admin tools to set ACLs.

activities.activity_name: U3 - Configure XD for secure ZK
activities.activity_description: Update Spring XD configuration (servers, admin, containers) to enable secure ZK connection, propagate credentials, and document the operator-facing configuration.
Integration tests verifying that unauthorized clients cannot read/write protected zNodes and that authorized clients succeed, including container startup under secure ZK.
Analyze the current Trigger interface, identify extension points, design a public SPI (interfaces, abstract base classes) that allows custom triggers without touching core code.
Refactor existing triggers to use the new SPI, add interfaces/abstract base classes, and update dependency injection to allow custom Trigger beans to be picked up.
Unit tests for the new SPI and a sample custom trigger test verifying it is discovered and invoked correctly by the runtime.
Choose a simple but representative example (e.g., a file-based source) that exercises module options, message conversion, and packaging.
Implement the example custom source module including build/assembly so it can be deployed as a user-built module.
Author a step-by-step guide for creating custom modules, covering project setup, SPI usage, options, packaging, and deployment, using the example as the worked case.
Design Kafka sink options (brokers, topic, key serializer, partitioning strategy, ack mode) and decide whether to wrap the producer per module instance or share.
Implement the Kafka sink using the Kafka producer client, wire options, and handle send/flush lifecycle and error reporting.
Unit tests for payload-to-ProducerRecord mapping and an integration test against an embedded Kafka broker verifying messages are produced.

activities.activity_name: U7 - Investigate socket hang up error
activities.activity_description: Reproduce the 'grunt test:e2e' failure locally, capture logs from both server and protractor, and identify whether the issue is port reuse, process signaling, or protractor config.
Update Gruntfile and/or protractor configuration to ensure tests and server run together reliably (e.g., explicit ready signal, no premature shutdown, correct base URL).
Run the e2e suite end-to-end multiple times in a clean environment to confirm the socket hang up is resolved and tests are stable.
Update Spring XD build files to use Spring Boot 1.1.7 SNAPSHOT (resolve any transitive dependency conflicts) and verify the project still builds.

activities.activity_name: U8 - Configure HTTPS for Admin server
activities.activity_description: Enable Spring Boot's server.ssl.* configuration for the Admin server, document required keystore/truststore properties, and ensure REST endpoints are served over HTTPS.
Integration tests verifying that Admin REST endpoints are reachable over HTTPS and rejected over plain HTTP, and that clients with the configured truststore succeed.
End-to-end smoke tests that exercise combinations of the new modules (e.g., JDBC source -> Kafka sink) to confirm no regressions in the runtime.
Update reference documentation/wiki pages describing JDBC source, Redis sink, Kafka sink, ZK security, custom triggers, custom modules, and HTTPS configuration.
Self-review changes, address review feedback, fix defects discovered during integration testing, and clean up before final delivery.
